channel.title: TechCrunch AI Tag
channel.description: AI news and insights from TechCrunch

item.title: Microsoft won’t stop buying AI chips from Nvidia, AMD, even after launching its own, Nadella says
item.description: Microsoft says its own chip leapfrogs those made by other cloud providers like Amazon and Google. But it needs more.

item.title: The AI infrastructure boom shows no sign of slowing down
item.description: ASML’s record orders show chipmakers are still betting big on AI data centers.

item.title: Anthropic reportedly upped its latest raise to $20B
item.description: Anthropic looks to raise $20 billion at more than $300 billion valuation, according to reports.

item.title: Google’s more affordable AI Plus plan rolls out to all markets, including the US
item.description: Gemini 3 Pro and other AI tools are now available globally through the Google AI Plus plan, which is $7.99 per month in the United States.

item.title: YouTubers sue Snap for alleged copyright infringement in training its AI models
item.description: The YouTubers claim Snap, like others, used AI datasets meant for research and academic use to train its AI models.

item.title: Google Photos’ latest feature lets you meme yourself
item.description: The addition is meant to just be a fun way to explore your photos and experiment with Google's Gemini AI technology, and specifically Nano Banana.

item.title: Google DeepMind CEO is ‘surprised’ OpenAI is rushing forward with ads in ChatGPT
item.description: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis says the tech giant isn't pressuring him to insert ads into the AI chatbot experience.

item.title: Spotify brings AI-powered Prompted Playlists to the US and Canada
item.description: Now available in the US and Canada, Spotify's AI-powered Prompted Playlists let users describe what they want to hear using natural language commands.

item.title: Not to be outdone by OpenAI, Apple is reportedly developing an AI wearable
item.description: Should this wearable materialize, it could be released as early as 2027, according to a report on the device.

item.title: Todoist’s app now lets you add tasks to your to-do list by speaking to its AI
item.description: The feature, now public, lets you create to-do's and action items by speaking naturally to the app's AI.

item.title: YouTube will soon let creators make Shorts with their own AI likeness
item.description: YouTube Shorts viewers might soon see AI versions of their favorite creators when scrolling through their feeds.

item.title: Moxie Marlinspike has a privacy-conscious alternative to ChatGPT
item.description: Confer is designed to look and feel like ChatGPT or Claude, but your conversations can't be used for training or advertising.

item.title: VoiceRun nabs $5.5M to build a voice agent factory
item.description: VoiceRun, a startup that creates voice agents, raised $5.5 million in a round led by Flybridge.

item.title: Ring founder details the camera company’s ‘intelligent assistant’ era
item.description: AI is ushering in Ring’s next chapter, as the Amazon-owned video doorbell maker shifts toward becoming an “intelligent assistant.”

item.title: Amazon says 97% of its devices can support Alexa+
item.description: Amazon is counting on its Alexa footprint to help it gain traction in the consumer AI race.

item.title: Inside CES 2026’s “physical AI” takeover
item.description: After years of chatbots and image generators, AI is finally leaving the screen. At CES 2026, that shift became impossible to ignore.  The annual tech showcase in Las Vegas was dominated by “physical AI” and robotics, from Boston Dynamic’s newly redesigned Atlas humanoid robot to AI-powered ice makers (yes, really). The companies in attendance clearly want consumers […]

item.title: Gmail debuts a personalized AI Inbox, AI Overviews in search, and more
item.description: Gmail is also bringing several AI features that were previously available only to paid users to all users.

item.title: AMD unveils new AI PC processors for general use and gaming at CES
item.description: AMD announced the latest version of its AI-powered PC chips designed for a variety of tasks, from gaming to content creation and multitasking.

item.title: Google previews new Gemini features for TV at CES 2026
item.description: Google TV will let you ask Gemini to find and edit your photos, adjust your TV settings, and more.

item.title: European banks plan to cut 200,000 jobs as AI takes hold
item.description: The bloodletting will hit hardest in back-office operations, risk management, and compliance.
